name: Official everything server
whyItMatters: Exercises tools, prompts, and resources in one official reference server.
reproductionNotes: Zero-config official package; useful as a broad protocol baseline.

name: Official sequential thinking server
whyItMatters: Small official tools server that makes schema readability easy to inspect.
reproductionNotes: Zero-config official package.

name: Official memory server
whyItMatters: Memory tools are agent-facing state; their schemas and write behavior should be visible before use.
reproductionNotes: Zero-config official package.

name: Official filesystem server
whyItMatters: Filesystem tools need harmless test roots and clear read/write boundaries.
reproductionNotes: Runs against the checked-in harmless fixture directory.

name: Filesystem MCP server
whyItMatters: Filesystem MCP is a core agent trust boundary because it exposes read, write, edit, delete, and directory traversal tools.
reproductionNotes: Safety Index generation creates an empty temporary directory for the server root and sanitizes that path from public artifacts.

name: Context7
whyItMatters: Documentation retrieval tools can return untrusted text into agent context.
reproductionNotes: Zero-config public package.

name: Promptopia
whyItMatters: Prompt-serving MCP packages need predictable prompt inventory and startup behavior.
reproductionNotes: Uses the checked-in prompt fixture through package defaults.

name: Ref tools
whyItMatters: Developer tools become agent dependencies when wired into coding workflows.
reproductionNotes: Zero-config public package.

name: Git MCP Server
whyItMatters: Coding agents often need Git context and can cause real repository changes if tool boundaries are unclear.
reproductionNotes: Zero-config public package. Keep tool invocation read-only unless a harmless fixture repository is added.

name: Official GitHub MCP server
whyItMatters: Exposes 26 tools to agents, including file writes, branch creation, issue/PR creation, and PR merges across any repo a token can reach — high-stakes write access that needs a visible boundary before an agent is trusted with it.
reproductionNotes: Zero-config package; tool listing succeeds without a real GitHub token, so this check is safe to run in CI. Note: npm currently flags this package as deprecated/no longer supported by the publisher — treat this target as compatibility evidence, not an endorsement of the package's maintenance status.

name: UI5 MCP Server
whyItMatters: UI5 agents can scaffold applications, run UI5-specific analysis, and fetch framework guidance, so teams need reproducible evidence before trusting the tool surface.
reproductionNotes: Zero-config public package; tool listing works without private credentials or a project fixture.

name: OpenTofu MCP server
whyItMatters: Infrastructure tools can influence production configuration and should have reviewable MCP surfaces.
reproductionNotes: Zero-config public package.

name: Puppeteer MCP server
whyItMatters: Browser automation gives agents navigation, page state, and sometimes code-evaluation powers.
reproductionNotes: Intentional browser evaluation is suppressed so remaining findings stay readable.

name: BrowserMCP
whyItMatters: Browser-control servers need visible tool boundaries before agents drive real browsing sessions.
reproductionNotes: Zero-config public package.

name: Microsoft Playwright MCP
whyItMatters: Popular browser automation servers need explicit review around navigation, screenshots, and code evaluation.
reproductionNotes: Zero-config public package; security findings represent policy-review prompts, not a vulnerability claim.

name: AntV chart MCP server
whyItMatters: Visualization servers produce files or structured outputs agents may pass into workflows.
reproductionNotes: Zero-config public package.

name: ExecuteAutomation Playwright MCP
whyItMatters: A public browser automation package that fails basic listing checks shows why reproducible readiness evidence matters.
reproductionNotes: Evaluated as a public package; current result should be treated as a maintainer conversation starter.

name: Flux159 Kubernetes MCP server
whyItMatters: Kubernetes MCP servers can expose cluster mutation, pod exec, manifest apply/delete, and broad kubectl command surfaces to agents.
reproductionNotes: Zero-config public package. Evaluated without cluster credentials; findings are metadata and schema boundary prompts, not exploit claims.

name: Chrome DevTools MCP
whyItMatters: Coding agents may use Chrome DevTools MCP to inspect pages, network state, console output, and browser behavior before making changes.
reproductionNotes: Zero-config public package; browser-control findings should be treated as policy-review prompts, not vulnerability claims.

name: Official Slack MCP server
whyItMatters: Slack MCP servers can expose channel history, message posting, and workspace search capabilities to agents.
reproductionNotes: Schema-only evaluation; full tool invocation requires a Slack token.

name: Official Google Drive MCP server
whyItMatters: Google Drive agents can read, write, search, and manage permissions on cloud documents the token can reach.
reproductionNotes: Schema-only evaluation; full tool invocation requires Google OAuth credentials.

name: Anthropic MongoDB MCP server
whyItMatters: MongoDB MCP servers can expose collection queries, document CRUD, and index management to agents.
reproductionNotes: Schema-only evaluation; full tool invocation requires a MongoDB connection string.

name: Anthropic Cloudflare MCP server
whyItMatters: Cloudflare MCP servers can expose DNS records, Workers, KV stores, and deployment pipelines to agents.
reproductionNotes: Schema-only evaluation; full tool invocation requires Cloudflare API credentials.

name: Anthropic Qdrant MCP server
whyItMatters: Qdrant MCP servers can expose vector search, collection management, and point CRUD to agents.
reproductionNotes: Schema-only evaluation; full tool invocation requires a Qdrant cluster URL and API key.

name: Anthropic Vercel AI SDK MCP server
whyItMatters: Vercel AI SDK MCP servers can expose project management, deployment triggers, and AI model configuration to agents.
reproductionNotes: Schema-only evaluation; full tool invocation may require Vercel API credentials.

name: Anthropic Tavily Search MCP server
whyItMatters: Tavily search MCP servers can return untrusted web search results directly into agent context.
reproductionNotes: Schema-only evaluation; full tool invocation may require a Tavily API key.

name: Stripe MCP
whyItMatters: Stripe tools can create customers, process payments, and manage subscriptions — financial mutation surfaces that need visible boundaries.
reproductionNotes: Schema-only; requires Stripe API key for full scan. Tool listing exposes payment operations.

name: Notion MCP
whyItMatters: Notion MCP servers can read, write, and search across workspace pages, databases, and comments.
reproductionNotes: Schema-only; requires Notion API integration token for full scan.

name: Linear MCP
whyItMatters: Linear MCP servers expose issue creation, team management, and cycle tracking to agents.
reproductionNotes: Schema-only; requires Linear API key for full scan.

name: Figma MCP
whyItMatters: Figma MCP servers can expose design files, components, and styles to agents for design-to-code workflows.
reproductionNotes: Schema-only; requires Figma access token for full scan.

name: Firecrawl MCP
whyItMatters: Firecrawl MCP servers expose web scraping, crawling, and content extraction tools that can pull untrusted content into agent context.
reproductionNotes: May work without auth for tool listing; full crawl operations require a Firecrawl API key.

name: Exa Search MCP
whyItMatters: Exa MCP servers return web search and crawling results into agent context from untrusted sources.
reproductionNotes: Schema-only; full search requires an Exa API key.

name: Sentry MCP
whyItMatters: Sentry MCP servers expose error, performance, and release data to agents, which can reveal sensitive stack traces and PII fields.
reproductionNotes: Schema-only; requires Sentry auth token for full scan.

name: Neon MCP
whyItMatters: Neon MCP servers can provision databases, manage branches, and run SQL — cloud database operations with production implications.
reproductionNotes: Schema-only; requires Neon API key and project ID for full scan.

name: Supabase MCP
whyItMatters: Supabase MCP servers can manage tables, run SQL, manage auth users, and control Edge Functions — broad backend control surface.
reproductionNotes: Schema-only; requires Supabase access token for full scan.

name: Docker MCP
whyItMatters: Docker MCP servers expose container run, exec, and image management tools — container-level command execution is a high-trust boundary.
reproductionNotes: Schema-only; requires Docker Desktop running for full scan. Tool listing may succeed without a running daemon.

name: Official PostgreSQL MCP server
whyItMatters: PostgreSQL MCP servers can run arbitrary SQL queries against connected databases — a high-trust data mutation surface.
reproductionNotes: Scanned with dummy connection string for schema discovery. Full query execution requires a real PostgreSQL connection. Note: npm flags this package as deprecated by the publisher.

name: Official SQLite MCP server
whyItMatters: SQLite MCP servers can grant agents read/write/query access to local database files with SQL execution capabilities.
reproductionNotes: Package not published on npm (404). Available in the servers monorepo. Use community packages like mcp-sqlite or build from source.

name: Official Fetch MCP server
whyItMatters: Fetch MCP servers can retrieve arbitrary web content and feed it into agent context — a prompt injection and content trust boundary.
reproductionNotes: Package not published on npm (404). Available in the servers monorepo. Use community packages like mcp-fetch-server or build from source.

name: Official Brave Search MCP server
whyItMatters: Brave Search MCP servers return web and local search results into agent context — untrusted content ingestion vector.
reproductionNotes: Scanned with dummy API key for schema/tool discovery. Full search execution requires a valid Brave Search API key. Note: npm flags this package as deprecated by the publisher.

name: Official GitLab MCP server
whyItMatters: GitLab MCP servers expose repository operations, merge requests, issues, and CI pipeline controls — high-stakes write access across repos.
reproductionNotes: Scanned with dummy token for schema/tool discovery. Server responds but tools have schema validation issues preventing full listing. Note: npm flags this package as deprecated by the publisher.

name: Anthropic Gmail MCP server
whyItMatters: Gmail MCP servers can read, send, archive, and manage emails on behalf of users — high-stakes message access that needs visible boundaries before agents are trusted with inbox control.
reproductionNotes: Schema-only evaluation; requires Gmail OAuth credentials. Note: @anthropic/mcp-server-gmail has not been published to npm. Community equivalent: gmail-mcp.

name: Anthropic Jina AI MCP server
whyItMatters: Jina AI MCP servers can perform web search and content reading — untrusted content ingestion into agent context.
reproductionNotes: Schema-only evaluation; requires Jina AI API key. Note: @anthropic/mcp-server-jina has not been published to npm. Community equivalent: jina-mcp-tools.

name: Anthropic Google Sheets MCP server
whyItMatters: Google Sheets MCP servers can read, write, and query spreadsheet data — agents with sheet access can modify business-critical data.
reproductionNotes: Schema-only evaluation; requires Google Sheets OAuth credentials. Note: @anthropic/mcp-server-google-sheets has not been published to npm. Community equivalent: google-sheets-mcp.

name: Anthropic Google Calendar MCP server
whyItMatters: Google Calendar MCP servers can create, read, update, and delete calendar events — agents can schedule meetings and modify availability.
reproductionNotes: Schema-only evaluation; requires Google Calendar OAuth credentials. Note: @anthropic/mcp-server-google-calendar has not been published to npm. Community equivalent: @cocal/google-calendar-mcp.

name: Anthropic Google Tasks MCP server
whyItMatters: Google Tasks MCP servers can create, list, update, and delete user tasks — agents can manage personal task lists with real user data.
reproductionNotes: Schema-only evaluation; requires Google Tasks OAuth credentials. Note: @anthropic/mcp-server-google-tasks has not been published to npm. Community equivalent: @overlay-one/google-tasks-mcp-server.

name: Anthropic HuggingFace MCP server
whyItMatters: HuggingFace MCP servers can access models, datasets, and inference endpoints — agents could download or interact with ML artifacts.
reproductionNotes: Schema-only evaluation; requires HuggingFace API token. Note: @anthropic/mcp-server-huggingface has not been published to npm. Community equivalent: huggingface-mcp-server.

name: Anthropic Reddit MCP server
whyItMatters: Reddit MCP servers can browse posts, search content, and interact with subreddits — agents could post or retrieve content from social platforms.
reproductionNotes: Schema-only evaluation; requires Reddit API credentials. Note: @anthropic/mcp-server-reddit has not been published to npm. Community equivalent: reddit-mcp.

name: Anthropic OneSignal MCP server
whyItMatters: OneSignal MCP servers can send push notifications, manage segments, and configure messaging campaigns — agent-triggered notifications to real users is a high-stakes boundary.
reproductionNotes: Schema-only evaluation; requires OneSignal API credentials. Note: @anthropic/mcp-server-onesignal has not been published to npm. No community MCP equivalent found as of this writing.

name: Anthropic Clay MCP server
whyItMatters: Clay MCP servers can access contact data, enrichment, and relationship intelligence — agents could read or modify CRM records with personal and business contact data.
reproductionNotes: Schema-only evaluation; requires Clay API credentials. Note: @anthropic/mcp-server-clay has not been published to npm. Community equivalent: @clayhq/clay-mcp.
